subject: math
title: E-Math trigonometry: ratios and the sine rule
objectives: Name the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse for an angle in a right-angled triangle
Use SOH CAH TOA to find sine, cosine and tangent ratios
Use the sine rule to find an unknown side in any triangle

definitions.meaning: The ratio opposite over hypotenuse for an angle in a right-angled triangle: in the 3-4-5 triangle, sin theta = 3/5 = 0.6 (the SOH part of the card).
The ratio adjacent over hypotenuse for an angle in a right-angled triangle: in the 3-4-5 triangle, cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8 (the CAH part of the card).
The ratio opposite over adjacent for an angle in a right-angled triangle: in the 3-4-5 triangle, tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75 (the TOA part of the card).
The longest side of a right-angled triangle, across from the right angle: length 5 in the 3-4-5 triangle.
The side across from the angle you are working with: length 3 for angle theta in the 3-4-5 triangle.
The side next to the angle you are working with, other than the hypotenuse: length 4 for angle theta in the 3-4-5 triangle.
The rule a / sin A = b / sin B, linking each side of any triangle with the sine of its opposite angle, used when there is no right angle.

mechanismSteps: Meet the 3-4-5 triangle: name the sides from angle theta first - opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = 5 - then sine is opposite over hypotenuse, sin theta = 3/5 = 0.6.
Cosine and tangent join the card: cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8 (adjacent over hypotenuse) and tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75 (opposite over adjacent) - read the whole card as SOH CAH TOA.
The sine rule for any triangle: a / sin A = b / sin B pairs each side with its opposite angle, so with a = 4, A = 30 degrees and B = 60 degrees, b comes out to about 6.93.
A common mistake: do not flip tangent: the flipped ratio 4/3 = 1.33 is taller than the whole, while the correct TOA ratio 3/4 = 0.75 sits properly inside it.
workedExample: Use the sine rule to find side b. In the triangle, side a = 4 is opposite angle A = 30 degrees, and angle B = 60 degrees. Write the rule: a / sin A = b / sin B, so 4 / sin 30 degrees = b / sin 60 degrees. Rearrange: b = (4 x sin 60 degrees) / sin 30 degrees = (4 x 0.8660) / 0.5 = 6.928, so b is about 6.93. Check: the side opposite the larger angle (60 degrees) is longer than the side opposite 30 degrees, and 6.93 is greater than 4, so the size makes sense.

trap.explanation: Opposite and adjacent swap places under pressure. Always read TOA: tan is opposite over adjacent. For the 3-4-5 triangle that means tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75, never 4/3.
